text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - DTB Bund futures penetrated the magic 102-level for the first time ever during the morning and dealers said the contract could go as high as 102.25 over the day. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.65, up 1.01 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - The December UK gilt future pushed steadily higher after breaking its old contract high of 111-17, spurred on by surging Bunds. And dealers said with the Bund rally likely to continue next week, gilts would be well supported on an absolute basis, but would struggle to keep up on relative terms. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-29/32, up 30/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures were near their highs in early afternoon, ignoring a weak franc, driven by hopes of interest rate easing and a powerful performance by Bunds. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.16, up 0.88 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt futures charged to fresh record highs in late European trading, while the lira, finishing its first week back in the ERM, was up in territory not seen for more than two years. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.03, up 1.26 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened moderately higher, ahead of what most expect to be just about the quietest session of the year. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 116-7/32, up 29/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.37 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese government bond futures ended the session down in thin, technical trade. The outgoing December contract closed down 0.10 at 126.15. The December has effectively lost its benchmark status as its turnover fell below that of the March. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 126.35, up 0.10 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market came to a virtual standstill caught between the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday and the weekend. Spain's Istituto de Credito Oficial (ICO) is expected to launch a $500 million five-year Eurobond next week. Meanwhile Spain is said to be eyeing the mark sector. Israel hits London next Wednesday ahead of the launch of a $200 million Eurobond via Merrill Lynch, traders say. J.P. Morgan is said to be launching a $200 million 10-year Eurobond for state-owned Slovak water utility.
